steps.what: Read outbound volumes for the plant.
Walk the ground for the plant distribution centers.
Choose layouts for the plant distribution centers.
Issue the layout to the project file.

tasks.design: Volumes come from {ERP}. The analyst walks the ground and chooses the layout. {PROJECT} receives it only after that choice.
tasks.previous_blocker: Centers were sketched from a volume sheet without a current walk.
tasks.enabler_now: The volume file can be read before anyone travels.
tasks.still_hard: A layout that ignores a door, a slope or a neighbour is not a design.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst sees the constraint the volume file does not name.
tasks.altitude: The walk and the layout choice stay. Filing the chosen layout does not.

reach.task: Turn the layout into a buildable drawing
reach.learn: Which site notes are verified and which are not

evidence.claim: A volume or a rate can be summed from fields. A site walk and a promise to a customer cannot.

assumptions: Focal role is the logistics analyst. Boundary: from volumes and a walk to an issued layout. Construction is out of scope.
Test the existing {ERP} view before a custom extract.
Structured fields are plant id, weekly volume and a constraint seen on the walk. Fallback: a constraint with no photo or measure is marked unverified.
EU data-protection rules apply. Monitoring named people needs works-council consent where national rules require it.
unknowns: Whether the ground may be walked before the layout is requested.
research_questions: How often the walk removes the option the volume sheet preferred.

already_counted.description: Choosing the layout after the walk

incremental.description: Keep volume definitions aligned with the plants in scope

approvals.approved_version: layout the analyst chose after the walk

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The volume read and the filing are saved. The walk and the choice stay. The low case is a site the analyst has not walked.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Pull contractual commitments and customer specifications.
Compare commitment dates with the logistics plan.
Flag support requirements the contract does not cover.
Judge which gaps the commitments actually create.
Check the review note before it is sent.
Send the review to the contract owner.

tasks.design: {ERP} compares commitment dates with the plan and lists support the contract does not cover. The analyst judges the gaps. {EMAIL} sends the note only after that check.
tasks.previous_blocker: Contracts and the operating plan were read in different weeks.
tasks.enabler_now: Dates and named requirements can be compared once both are fields.
tasks.still_hard: A date match can still hide a service the customer believes was promised.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst can read what the specification implies and the date field does not.

ambition.what: Review a contract when the plan changes, not only at renewal.

tasks.altitude: Judging the gap stays. The date comparison does not.

reach.task: Renegotiate a commitment the review has flagged
reach.learn: Which requirement is uncovered and which is only slow

evidence.claim: A volume or a rate can be summed from fields. A site walk and a promise to a customer cannot.

assumptions: Focal role is the logistics analyst. Boundary: from the contract and the plan to a sent review. Renegotiation stays with the contract owner.
Test the existing {ERP} view before a custom extract.
Structured fields are commitment id, date, specification clause and plan lane. Fallback: a scanned clause with no date is listed for the analyst, not guessed.
EU data-protection rules apply. Monitoring named people needs works-council consent where national rules require it.
unknowns: Which contracts the analyst is allowed to read in full.
research_questions: How often a flagged gap is a wording issue rather than a real miss.

already_counted.description: Judging which contract gaps are real

incremental.description: Keep clause types aligned with the contracts in force

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Clean dates save the comparison and the send. The judgement stays. The low case is a scanned contract with no dates.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Watch the conveyor and the tracking points.
List what the warehousing software already records.
Compare missed scans with the inventory record.
Evaluate whether the technology closes those misses.
Write the evaluation for the operations lead.

tasks.design: The analyst watches the conveyor. {ERP} compares missed scans with the inventory record. The evaluation says whether the technology closes the misses the watch saw.
tasks.previous_blocker: Technology was judged from a vendor demonstration, not from missed scans on this floor.
tasks.enabler_now: Scan logs and inventory records can be compared without retyping.
tasks.still_hard: A scanner that works in a demo can fail at a corner the analyst has to see.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst has watched the point where labels are missed.
tasks.altitude: Watching the floor and judging the technology stay. The miss count does not.

reach.task: Confirm which scan points fail on a shift
reach.learn: Which misses the log shows and which the watch added

evidence.claim: A volume or a rate can be summed from fields. A site walk and a promise to a customer cannot.

assumptions: Focal role is the logistics analyst. Boundary: from a watch and the scan log to an evaluation note. Buying the technology is a different task.
Test the existing {ERP} view before a custom extract.
Structured fields are scan point, miss count and inventory id. The scan log produces the counts. Fallback: a miss seen only on the watch is typed and marked unverified.
EU data-protection rules apply. Monitoring named people needs works-council consent where national rules require it.
unknowns: Whether the scan log is complete for the shifts being judged.
research_questions: How often a watched miss never appears in the log.

already_counted.description: Evaluating the technology after the watch

incremental.description: Keep scan-point names aligned with the floor

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A complete scan log saves the comparison. The watch and the evaluation stay. The low case is a shift whose misses are not in the log.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: State the service the customers need solved.
Draft logistics solutions inside that constraint.

loop.purpose: Draft solutions from the customer's stated constraint.
loop.check: Each option names a cost and a limit.
loop.stop: Stop after two options or when a limit is missing.
loop.why_not_simpler: A catalogue cannot see the constraint this customer just stated.

steps.what: Propose the solutions in the customer meeting.

tasks.design: The customer states the constraint. One draft in {DOCS} offers two logistics solutions inside it. The analyst proposes them in the meeting and does not send a commitment.
tasks.previous_blocker: Proposals were written before the customer had stated the constraint.
tasks.enabler_now: A draft can be prepared once the constraint is a field.
tasks.still_hard: Committing a price or a date in the meeting is still a commercial decision.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst hears what the customer will not put in a form.

ambition.what: Prepare a first option for a customer the team has not served before, still proposed in person.

tasks.altitude: The meeting stays. The blank first draft does not. Customer time is not saved.

reach.task: Commit a price after the meeting
reach.learn: Which options were proposed and which limits the customer set

evidence.claim: A volume or a rate can be summed from fields. A site walk and a promise to a customer cannot.

assumptions: Focal role is the logistics analyst. Boundary: from a stated constraint to a proposal made in the meeting. The customer's time is not saved. No option is sent as a commitment.
Test the existing {ERP} view before a custom extract.
Structured fields are constraint, cost and limit. The customer states them. Fallback: a limit not stated is not filled with a default.
EU data-protection rules apply. Monitoring named people needs works-council consent where national rules require it.
unknowns: Which customers will state a constraint before the meeting.
research_questions: How often the meeting rejects both drafted options.

already_counted.description: Preparing the draft the meeting will use

incremental.description: Keep standard limits current so a draft does not invent one

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Only the draft is partly saved. The meeting stays in full. Customer time is not saved. The low case is a customer who will not state the constraint ahead.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Site walks, contract judgement and what is promised to a customer stay with the analyst. Volume sums and document drafts do not.
reach: Contract owners, on which commitment fields a gap list needs.
Facilities engineers, on which site facts a layout needs.
skills_to_grow: Refusing a saving that the site cannot run.
role.ambitious_version: A proposal to a customer names the constraint, the option and the person who may commit.
